newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks ease at opening as bonds weaken.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks ease at opening as bonds weaken.

text.p: Australian stocks eased slightly at the opening on Wednesday as local bond futures weaken, ignoring further gains on Wall Street.
The All Ordinaries index eased off Tuesday's record close and after half an hour of trading the index was 2.5 points lower at 2,510.3.
Trading was thin with only A$114.07 million (US$88.52 million) worth of business put through the market early.
Brokers said the market is likely to trade in a narrow range for the rest of the day as the small rise in New York was not enough to give positive impetus to the market.
Resources were steady after flat metal prices and a weaker gold price.

"The bonds are off a bit and that seems to be weighing on sentiment in the stocks at the moment," one Sydney-based dealer said. The Australian 10-year bond futures was seven basis points weaker at 92.195.
The debt futures weakened after the Reserve Bank made no annoucement on policy after Tuesday's board meeting as the market had set itself up for a surprise easing.
Brokers said the market also had been a bit shy about staying above the 2,500 level.
"After such a move, there comes some consolidation which makes everyone a bit nervous," the dealer said.
Banks shares extended their recent rise ahead of the round of half-year results due out over the next couple of weeks.

Newspaper group John Fairfax shares eased on profit-taking after its recent strong rise on renewed speculation that the company would be taken over following an expected easing in Australia's media ownership laws.
